title: AI Model Card Minimum Elements: EU AI Act Article 11 & Annex IV Checklist
context: 2026-08-29 engine cycle -- answer-first practical compliance seed; model card generation is mandatory for high-risk AI under Art 11, with Annex IV specifying 11 minimum documentation elements.
body: Under the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), high-risk AI system providers must draw up and maintain technical documentation — what the market calls a model card — before placing the system on the market. Article 11 sets the obligation; Annex IV lists the minimum elements. Practically, a compliant model card must cover eleven items. (1) A general description including intended purpose, the person/system it represents, version, and relevant hardware/software environment. (2) A detailed description of the system design: architecture, input/output specification, data format, development methodology including where training or fine-tuning used pre-trained models and how those were used. (3) Description of training data: provenance, scope, main characteristics, how collected/selected, labelling procedures, data cleaning. (4) Human oversight measures under Art 14: built-in tools enabling overseers to understand, monitor, interpret, and override. (5) Foreseeable risks to health, safety, fundamental rights — including risks from misuse and the results of the risk management system under Art 9. (6) Accuracy metrics: relevant accuracy and robustness levels together with any limitations. (7) Discriminatory impact: reasonably foreseeable unintended outcomes and sources of bias that may lead to discrimination. (8) Cybersecurity assessment: resilience against adversarial manipulation and attempts to exploit vulnerabilities. (9) Performance metrics used: specification of the metrics for measuring accuracy, robustness, and compliance with Art 15. (10) Logging capabilities under Art 12: how events are automatically recorded during operation. (11) For general-purpose AI models (Art 53): a publicly available sufficiently detailed summary of training content. Beyond the EU, the ISO/IEC 42001 management system and the NIST AI RMF both reference model-card-style transparency records. For a provider, the practical move is to produce a machine-readable card (JSON Schema or SPDX AI Profile) and sign it with a verified measurement credential so it survives an audit without re-litigation of each element.
references: NIST AI RMF 1.0 — Map, Measure, Manage, Govern
